parsedVerdict.reasoning: The unit fails on two counts: it doesn't use its abstractions consistently, and it repeats a rule. In GateLog.scanned, the code ignores the PrismaService it was given in its constructor and creates a new PrismaClient instead. The other method in the same class, busiestGate, uses the injected this.prisma, so even GateLog is inconsistent with itself. Across the module, BoxOffice reaches persistence only through domain stores (EventStore, TicketStore) and builds domain objects (Event, Ticket). GateLog works directly on raw Prisma rows (prisma.scan). So the two files sit behind different boundaries. Scanning is also split across both files: BoxOffice.admit records the scan through TicketStore.markScanned, while GateLog.scanned writes a separate scan record through Prisma. Nothing connects the two, so 'a ticket was scanned' is recorded in two places. Finally, BoxOffice rebuilds an Event from stored data with the same six-argument constructor call in both purchase and listing. That mapping should live in one place.

violations.message: scanned() creates `new PrismaClient()` instead of using the injected PrismaService (this.prisma), skipping the class's own abstraction; busiestGate() uses this.prisma, so the two methods are inconsistent.

GateLog works directly on raw Prisma scan rows, while the rest of the module goes through domain stores and domain objects. It also records ticket scans separately from BoxOffice.admit/TicketStore.markScanned, so the same fact lives in two places.
The Event rebuild (`new Event(data.id, data.title, data.venueCapacity, data.seatsSold, data.startsAt, data.priceCents)`) is repeated in purchase() and listing() instead of living in one place.
